pairs: Audierunt autem hostes Judæ et Benjamin,
Now the enemies of Judah and of Benjamin heard that the sons of the captivity were building a temple to the Lord,
quia filii captivitatis ædificarent templum Domino Deo Israël:
et accedentes ad Zorobabel, et ad principes patrum,
And so, drawing near to Zerubbabel and to the leaders of the fathers,
quia ita ut vos, quærimus Deum vestrum:
for we seek your God just as you do. Behold,
ecce nos immolavimus victimas a diebus Asor Haddan regis Assur,
we have immolated victims to him from the days of Esarhaddon, king of Assyria,
et Josue, et reliqui principes patrum Israël:
and the rest of the leaders of the fathers of Israel said to them:
Non est vobis et nobis ut ædificemus domum Deo nostro,
“It is not for you to build the house of our God with us. Instead,
sed nos ipsi soli ædificabimus Domino Deo nostro,
we alone shall build to the Lord our God, just as Cyrus,
sicut præcepit nobis Cyrus rex Persarum.
the king of the Persians, has commanded us.”
Factum est igitur ut populus terræ impediret manus populi Judæ,
Therefore, it happened that the people of the land impeded the hands of the people of Judah,
and they troubled them in building.
Then they hired counselors against them,
ut destruerent consilium eorum omnibus diebus Cyri regis Persarum,
so that they might argue against their plan during all the days of Cyrus, king of Persia,
et usque ad regnum Darii regis Persarum.
even until the reign of Darius, king of the Persians.
at the beginning of his reign,
they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and of Jerusalem.
Et in diebus Artaxerxis scripsit Beselam,
And so, in the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam,
et reliqui qui erant in consilio eorum, ad Artaxerxem regem Persarum:
and the others who were in their council wrote to Artaxerxes, king of the Persians.
epistola autem accusationis scripta erat syriace, et legebatur sermone syro.
Now the letter of accusation was written in Syriac, and was being read in the Syrian language.
scripserunt epistolam unam de Jerusalem Artaxerxi regi,
the scribe, wrote one letter from Jerusalem to king Artaxerxes,
and the rest of their counselors, the judges,
and the rest of the nations,
quas transtulit Asenaphar magnus et gloriosus, et habitare eas fecit in civitatibus Samariæ, et in reliquis regionibus trans flumen in pace
whom the great and glorious Osnappar transferred and caused to live in the cities of Samaria and in the rest of the regions across the river in peace:
(This is a copy of the letter,
the men who are across the river,
Let it be known to the king,
qui ascenderunt a te ad nos,
that the Jews, who ascended from you to us,
venerunt in Jerusalem civitatem rebellem et pessimam,
have arrived in Jerusalem, a rebellious and most wicked city,
quam ædificant exstruentes muros ejus, et parietes componentes.
which they are building, constructing its ramparts and repairing the walls.
And now let be it known to the king,
quia si civitas illa ædificata fuerit,
that if this city will have been built up,
et usque ad reges hæc noxa perveniet.
and this loss will affect even the kings.
remembering the salt that we have eaten in the palace,
et quia læsiones regis videre nefas ducimus,
and because we are led to believe that it is a crime to see the king harmed,
we have therefore sent and reported to the king,
ut recenseas in libris historiarum patrum tuorum,
so that you may search in the books of the histories of your fathers,
and you may find written in the records,
and you may know that this city is a rebellious city,
and that it is harmful to the kings and the provinces,
and that wars were incited within it from the days of antiquity.
et bella concitantur in ea ex diebus antiquis:
quam ob rem et civitas ipsa destructa est.
Nuntiamus nos regi, quoniam si civitas illa ædificata fuerit,
We report to the king that if this city will have been built,
you will have no possession across the river.”
Verbum misit rex ad Reum Beelteem,
The king sent word to Rehum, the commander,
et ad reliquos, qui erant in consilio eorum habitatores Samariæ,
and to the rest who were in their council, to the inhabitants of Samaria,
and to the others across the river,
which you have sent to us,
has been read aloud before me.
And it was commanded by me,
and they searched and found that this city,
inveneruntque quoniam civitas illa a diebus antiquis adversum reges rebellat,
and that seditions and battles have been incited within it.
nam et reges fortissimi fuerunt in Jerusalem,
Then too, there have been very strong kings in Jerusalem,
qui et dominati sunt omni regioni quæ trans fluvium est:
who also ruled over the entire region which is across the river.
ut urbs illa non ædificetur donec si forte a me jussum fuerit.
so that this city may be not built, until perhaps there may be further orders from me.
See to it that you are not negligent in fulfilling this,
et paulatim crescat malum contra reges.
otherwise, little by little, the evil may increase against the kings.”
Itaque exemplum edicti Artaxerxis regis lectum est coram Reum Beelteem,
And so a copy of the edict of king Artaxerxes was read before Rehum, the commander,
et abierunt festini in Jerusalem ad Judæos,
And they went away hurriedly to Jerusalem, to the Jews.
et prohibuerunt eos in brachio et robore.
And they prohibited them by force and by strength.
Tunc intermissum est opus domus Domini in Jerusalem,
Then the work of the house of the Lord in Jerusalem was interrupted,
et non fiebat usque ad annum secundum regni Darii regis Persarum.
and it did not resume until the second year of the reign of Darius, the king of the Persians.
